key_insight: A small set of attention heads helps determine whether a multimodal AI follows visual or textual evidence when the two disagree. These “arbitration heads” offer a potential control point for steering that choice at inference time.
problem_solved: Multimodal models can favor text or images even when the preferred modality is less reliable for the task, producing unreliable answers under conflicting inputs.
method: Study model predictions when visual and textual inputs provide conflicting evidence.
Identify attention heads that causally influence whether predictions follow images or text.
Use these arbitration heads as the basis for lightweight inference-time control; the supplied abstract is truncated before implementation details.
impact: The findings suggest a targeted way to steer how multimodal models resolve contradictory evidence, rather than accepting their default modality preference. This could support more dependable applications, although performance results are not available in the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Conflict diagram: an image and a text statement give different answers to the same question.

paper_title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
paper_authors: Zhaoying Pan, Shenyu Lu, Jun Hui Wong, Junyi Chai, Xiaoqian Wang
